newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian pepper sizzles on tight supply.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian pepper sizzles on tight supply.

text.p: Malaysian pepper prices are sizzling on the international market, with a worldwide shortage of the spice pushing up rates by 30 to 40 percent in just two months, trade sources said on Friday.

White pepper from Malaysia's eastern Sarawak state -- the country's main growing area for pepper -- was priced on Friday at between $6,800 and $6,900 a tonne in the New York market for August/September shipment.
This was about 33 percent higher than the $5,100 to $5,200 a tonne fetched by Sarawak white pepper for July/August, traders in Kuching, the capital of Sarawak, said.
Sarawak black pepper was now trading in New York at around $5,400 to $5,500 a tonne for August/September, a premium of 38 to 40 percent from the $3,900 for July/August, said traders.
"We're seeing this rally because of the worldwide shortage in pepper supply," said a spokesman for the Pepper Marketing Board in Kuching.
"There has been lower production forecast from us, India, Indonesia and all others this year."
India is the largest producer of pepper in the world, followed by Indonesia, Malaysia, Vietnam and Brazil.
Indian traders said the country has forecast production at 55,000 tonnes for 1996/97 (November-October), compared to the 62,000 tonnes produced in 1995/96.
The inter-governmental International Pepper Community (IPC) has revised downwards its production forecast on Indonesia to 38,000 tonnes in 1997 from 39,200 tonnes in 1996.
Malaysia's production for 1997 was estimated at between 15,000 and 16,000 tonnes, close to 1996's output, the Pepper Marketing Board said.
"Actually, it's quite difficult to estimate the production because there are so many small growers in every nook and cranny of Sarawak," said the board's spokesman.
"Also, there are held-over stocks coming into the market, so the figure cannot be too accurate," he added.
The spokesman said exports of white pepper for the first seven months of the year totalled 10,684 tonnes, compared to the 6,574 tonnes in the same period of 1996.
Black pepper exports between January and July 1997 totalled 3,330 tonnes, compared to 2,584 tonnes in the corresponding period of 1996.
In Malaysia, black pepper trades at a premium over white pepper.
Sarawak black pepper was fetching around 9,000 ringgit a tonne for August/September, compared to 7,000 ringgit for July/August, traders said.
They said white pepper from Sarawak was quoted at around 1,400 ringgit for Aug/September, compared to 1,100 ringgit for July/August.
"It's more of a consumer choice in Malaysia -- black is more popular than white," said a trader.
